I'll help you embed a video in your MDX file. Based on the search results and Astro's documentation, there are a few ways to embed videos in MDX files.

Since MDX allows you to use HTML directly within your content, the simplest approach is to use the standard HTML `<video>` element or an `<iframe>` for services like YouTube or Vimeo.

Here are your options:

## 1. Using HTML directly in your MDX file

For a local video file:

```html
<video 
  src="/path/to/your/video.mp4" 
  controls 
  width="100%" 
  height="auto"
  poster="/path/to/thumbnail.jpg">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
```

For YouTube videos:

```html
<iframe 
  width="560" 
  height="315" 
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID" 
  title="YouTube video player" 
  frameborder="0" 
  allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" 
  allowfullscreen>
</iframe>
```

## 2. Creating a custom Video component

Alternatively, you can create a reusable Video component. This is especially useful if you plan to embed multiple videos with consistent styling.

Here's how you can create and use a custom Video component:

1. First, create a Video component:

---

```diff
- 
+ ---
+ interface Props {
+   src: string;
+   title?: string;
+   width?: string | number;
+   height?: string | number;
+   poster?: string;
+   controls?: boolean;
+   autoplay?: boolean;
+   loop?: boolean;
+   muted?: boolean;
+   type?: 'youtube' | 'vimeo' | 'local';
+ }
+ 
+ const {
+   src,
+   title = '',
+   width = '100%',
+   height = 'auto',
+   poster = '',
+   controls = true,
+   autoplay = false,
+   loop = false,
+   muted = false,
+   type = 'local'
+ } = Astro.props;
+ 
+ // Extract video ID from YouTube or Vimeo URLs
+ function getVideoId(url: string, type: string): string {
+   if (type === 'youtube') {
+     // Handle both youtube.com/watch?v=ID and youtu.be/ID formats
+     const regex = /(?:youtube\.com\/watch\?v=|youtu\.be\/)([^&\s]+)/;
+     const match = url.match(regex);
+     return match ? match[1] : url;
+   } else if (type === 'vimeo') {
+     // Handle vimeo.com/ID format
+     const regex = /vimeo\.com\/(\d+)/;
+     const match = url.match(regex);
+     return match ? match[1] : url;
+   }
+   return url;
+ }
+ 
+ const videoId = type !== 'local' ? getVideoId(src, type) : '';
+ ---
+ 
+ {type === 'local' ? (
+   <video 
+     src={src} 
+     width={width} 
+     height={height} 
+     poster={poster}
+     controls={controls} 
+     autoplay={autoplay}
+     loop={loop}
+     muted={muted}
+     title={title}
+   >
+     <slot />
+     Your browser does not support the video tag.
+   </video>
+ ) : type === 'youtube' ? (
+   <iframe
+     width={width}
+     height={height === 'auto' ? '315' : height}
+     src={`https://www.youtube.com/embed/${videoId}`}
+     title={title || "YouTube video player"}
+     frameborder="0"
+     allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
+     allowfullscreen
+   ></iframe>
+ ) : (
+   <iframe
+     width={width}
+     height={height === 'auto' ? '315' : height}
+     src={`https://player.vimeo.com/video/${videoId}`}
+     title={title || "Vimeo video player"}
+     frameborder="0"
+     allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture"
+     allowfullscreen
+   ></iframe>
+ )}
+ 
+ <style>
+   video, iframe {
+     max-width: 100%;
+     border-radius: 0.25rem;
+   }
+ </style> 
```

Now that I've created a Video component for you, here's how you can use it in your MDX file:

## Using the Video Component in Your MDX File

Now you can import and use the Video component in your MDX file. Here are some examples:

### For a local video:

```mdx
---
title: "6. Child's Play"
description: "Book Review: Folk Illusions"
date: 2025-03-02
authors: 
  - name: "Weaver"
draft: true
tags: 
  - volitional goosebumps
  - ASMR
  - chills
  - frission
bluesky_post_uri: "https://bsky.app/profile/phenomenal.ink/post/"
---
import Sidenote from '../../components/Sidenote.astro';
import Video from '../../components/Video.astro';

// Your content here...

<Video 
  src="/videos/your-video-file.mp4" 
  poster="/images/thumbnail.jpg" 
  width="100%" 
  controls
/>

// Continue with your content...
```

### For a YouTube video:

```mdx
<Video 
  type="youtube" 
  src="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ" 
  title="Example YouTube Video" 
  width="100%" 
  height="400"
/>
```

### For a Vimeo video:

```mdx
<Video 
  type="vimeo" 
  src="https://vimeo.com/123456789" 
  title="Example Vimeo Video" 
  width="100%" 
  height="400"
/>
```

## Alternative: Direct HTML in MDX

If you prefer not to use the component for a specific case, you can still use HTML directly in your MDX file:

```mdx
<video src="/videos/your-video.mp4" controls width="100%">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>

<!-- Or for YouTube -->
<iframe 
  width="560" 
  height="315" 
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" 
  title="YouTube video player" 
  frameborder="0" 
  allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" 
  allowfullscreen>
</iframe>
```

The Video component I created offers more flexibility and consistent styling, but direct HTML works perfectly fine in MDX files as well. Choose whichever approach works best for your specific needs.
